title: How bees see the world
summary: Get a feel for how a bee's vision differs from ours, and why that matters for flowers.
learningObjectives: Name a few ways bee vision differs from human vision
keyTakeaways: Bees do not see red the way we do
Flowers have patterns we cannot see
explanation:
Imagine a garden through different eyes. A bee's eyes are made of thousands of tiny lenses, and they respond to a **different slice of light** than ours.

The most surprising difference is ultraviolet. Many flowers carry markings that are invisible to us but stand out to bees, a bit like landing lights on a runway. This is a light, curious tour, not a test.

blocks.title: Ideas worth knowing

ideas.why: Flowers that look plain to us can show bold patterns to a bee.

ideas.idea: Bees are not good at seeing red
ideas.why: Red flowers look dark or dull to them, which is why many bee-visited flowers are yellow, blue or purple.
Thousands of tiny lenses build up a picture that is detailed in motion but not sharp like ours.

ideas.idea: Bees use the pattern of polarised light in the sky
ideas.why: It helps them find direction even when the sun is hidden.

wonder: What would a garden look like if you could only see ultraviolet?
Why might flowers have evolved patterns that only their visitors can see?
blocks.note: A starting point; follow your curiosity from here.

commonMistakes: Thinking bees see the world just like us but in other colours
Assuming all insects see the same way

quiz.question: Which kind of light can bees see that people cannot?
quiz.explanation: Bees see ultraviolet, which people cannot.

quiz.question: Why might a red flower look dull to a bee?
options: Bees do not see red the way we do
quiz.explanation: Bees lack the red sensitivity people have, so red looks dark to them.

socraticChallenge.scenario: You photograph a plain-looking yellow flower and an ultraviolet camera shows a dark centre.
socraticChallenge.question: What might that pattern be for?
socraticChallenge.idealAnswer: It likely guides bees towards the nectar, like a landing target that only they can see.

exercises.prompt: In two sentences, explain to a friend why some flowers have patterns we cannot see.
exercises.answer: Bees see ultraviolet light, so the patterns guide them to nectar, even though we cannot see them.

reviewCards.prompt: Which part of the spectrum can bees see that people cannot?
Why do some flowers have ultraviolet markings?
reviewCards.answer: They guide bees to the nectar.
